name: williams_r_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Williams %R with a 20-period lookback on 1-min bars identifies when price is at the extreme of its 20-bar range (below -90 or above -10). Unlike stochastic, Williams %R is unsmoothed, making it faster to react to turning points but also noisier. The key insight is combining %R extremes with a volume spike: when Williams %R < -90 AND volume is >2x its 20-bar SMA, it indicates a capitulation-style selloff that exhausts sellers. The volume spike distinguishes a genuine extreme from a quiet drift to the range bottom. The edge exists because Williams %R is less popular than RSI/Stochastic among Indian traders, reducing signal crowding, and the volume-spike confirmation is not standard practice.

long.confirmation: wr_slope > 0 (Williams %R turning up from extreme) AND close > open

short.confirmation: wr_slope < 0 (Williams %R turning down from extreme) AND close < open

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.signal_exit: exit if williams_r re-enters extreme zone (<-95 for longs, >-5 for shorts)

filters.volume_filter: volume spike > 2x on the extreme bar (essential for signal quality)
filters.trend_filter: VWAP proximity filter: only trade within ±1% of VWAP (avoid trending extremes)
other_filters: skip if williams_r has been in extreme zone for >5 consecutive bars (trending, not reverting)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — Williams %R is less crowded than RSI/Stochastic but conceptually similar

weaknesses: Williams %R is unsmoothed — very noisy on 1-min bars; extreme readings can occur on a single large bar
The volume spike requirement (2x) filters out many valid signals; conversely, volume spikes can be caused by a single block deal, not capitulation
Essentially the same signal as Stochastic(20,1,1) inverted — not truly independent from other oscillator-based strategies
prior_art: Williams %R by Larry Williams (1973). Standard TA indicator. Less popular than RSI/Stochastic in Indian markets, which is actually an advantage. Volume spike confirmation on oscillator extremes is discussed by Elder ('Trading for a Living'). The concept of capitulation volume at extremes is from Wyckoff methodology.
notes: Edge math: 0.57 * 25bps - 0.43 * 23bps = 14.25 - 9.9 = 4.35 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -6.65 bps. Negative. The volume spike filter is the key differentiator — without it, %R reversion is unprofitable. With strict volume spike filter, win rate may improve to 0.62+, which would give: 0.62*25 - 0.38*23 = 15.5 - 8.7 = 6.8 bps gross, still below costs. Best used as a composite signal component, not standalone.
